name: npmscan
description: Detect malicious, vulnerable, or typosquatted npm packages from a conversation. Search the npm registry, or compare 2-5 candidates side-by-side before adding a new dependency; inspect maintainers, install scripts, and Sigstore publish provenance before installing; audit a whole package.json/lockfile/SBOM/GitHub repo — including transitive dependencies, license compliance, and before/after PR diffs or npm audit output — against OSV.dev / GitHub Security Advisories / NIST NVD (with CISA KEV and FIRST EPSS enrichment); then get a prioritized remediation ranking, concrete incident-response playbooks, a CI-ready PASS/WARN/FAIL merge gate, safer-alternative suggestions, and a generated CycloneDX/SPDX SBOM — via npmscan.com's free, read-only MCP server.

interface.longDescription: Check npm packages for known vulnerabilities, malware, typosquats, maintainer takeovers, and risky install scripts before you install, upgrade, or ship them. Backed by npmscan.com's free, read-only MCP server (23 tools, no API key): npm registry search and side-by-side comparison, OSV.dev / GitHub Security Advisories / NIST NVD lookups enriched with CISA KEV and FIRST EPSS, Sigstore provenance and maintainer-history checks, whole-repo and transitive-dependency audits, license compliance, PR dependency diffs, npm audit enrichment, remediation ranking, and CycloneDX/SPDX SBOM generation. Bundles five skills: dependency-audit (audit a package.json, lockfile, SBOM, or GitHub repo), package-trust-check (is one package safe or compromised), new-dependency-evaluation (pick between candidate packages), incident-response (concrete playbooks for a flagged package), and ci-pr-gate (a deterministic PASS/WARN/FAIL merge verdict). Official page: https://npmscan.com
defaultPrompt: Check if the npm package lodash is safe to install
Audit the package.json in my project for vulnerabilities
Compare axios vs node-fetch before I add a dependency
